sources.title: Python FastAPI Tutorial: Build a REST API in 15 Minutes

steps.title: Install FastAPI and run hello world
steps.instructions: In an empty folder run `pip install fastapi uvicorn`, create main.py with `app = FastAPI()` and an `@app.get("/")` handler returning {"Hello": "World"}. Start it with `uvicorn main:app --reload` and open .

targets.caption: Create the FastAPI app instance
GET handler for the root path
Server is up; open this URL
JSON returned by the root route

explanations.topic: Uvicorn is the server that runs FastAPI apps
Path operation decorator for HTTP GET
uvicorn main:app means file name then app variable
--reload restarts the server on file changes

hints: Install both packages first: pip install fastapi uvicorn.
In main.py import FastAPI, create app = FastAPI(), then decorate a function with @app.get("/") that returns a dict.
Run uvicorn main:app --reload from the folder containing main.py, where main is the file name and app is the variable name.
common_mistakes: Installing only fastapi without uvicorn, so the uvicorn command is not found.
Running uvicorn from a different directory than main.py, which gives 'Could not import module "main"'.
Mismatching the app name, e.g. uvicorn main:App when the variable is app.
Writing main.py:app instead of main:app.
Forgetting the parentheses in FastAPI() or the leading slash in the route path.

steps.title: Add POST endpoint to create items
steps.instructions: Add a module-level `items = []` list and an `@app.post("/items")` function `create_item(item: str)` that appends the item and returns the list. Test with `curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'`.

targets.caption: Module-level list holding the items
POST endpoint at /items
item is read from the query string
POST request succeeded

explanations.topic: What routes are in FastAPI
POST request to the /items path
Plain function arguments become query parameters
Passing a query parameter with curl

hints: Create an empty list at module level (outside any function) so it persists between requests.
Decorate a new function with @app.post("/items") and give it a parameter `item: str`.
Inside the function call items.append(item) and return items.
common_mistakes: Putting `items = []` inside the function, so the list resets on every request.
Using @app.get instead of @app.post, so curl -X POST returns 405 Method Not Allowed.
Forgetting quotes around the URL in curl, so the shell mangles the `?` query string.
Sending the item as a JSON body instead of `?item=...`, giving a 422 'field required' error.
Not having uvicorn running (or not running it with --reload), so curl can't connect or the new route isn't picked up.

steps.title: Add GET endpoint for one item
steps.instructions: Add `@app.get("/items/{item_id}")` with `get_item(item_id: int)` returning `items[item_id]`. After the reload, POST two items again, then run `curl -X GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/0`.

targets.caption: New GET route with a path parameter
Type hint converts the path value to int
Fetch the first item by index

explanations.topic: Path parameters in curly brackets map to a function variable
Server reload resets the in-memory items list
Path value becomes the function argument
Type hints make FastAPI convert the parameter type

hints: Create a new route with the same @app.get decorator, putting the variable part of the path in curly brackets.
The name inside {} must match a parameter name of your function, e.g. def get_item(item_id: int).
Return items[item_id]. Without the int type hint the value arrives as a string and can't index a list.
After saving, the server reloads and the list is empty: POST a couple of items again before you curl /items/0.
common_mistakes: Path variable name in {} differs from the function parameter name, so FastAPI treats it as a query parameter and returns 422.
Omitting the int type hint, so indexing the list with a string raises TypeError (500).
Testing GET right after the reload without re-adding items, causing IndexError and an Internal Server Error.
Reusing the function name of another route, which silently shadows the earlier handler in the module.

steps.title: Raise 404 with HTTPException
steps.instructions: In main.py import `HTTPException` from fastapi and make get_item return the item only if `item_id < len(items)`, otherwise `raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found")`. Request a missing index like `curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/3` to see the 404 detail.

targets.caption: Import HTTPException from fastapi
Raise a 404 when the index is missing
The 404 detail for a missing item

explanations.topic: Why an internal server error isn't helpful for a missing item
HTTP status codes: client errors and 404 Not Found
Using the detail parameter to explain the error

hints: A missing item is a client error. FastAPI has a built-in exception for returning HTTP error codes.
Import HTTPException alongside FastAPI: `from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException`.
In get_item, check `if item_id < len(items):` and return the item. Otherwise `raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found")`.
common_mistakes: Using `return HTTPException(...)` instead of `raise`. That sends a 200 or a serialization error instead of a 404.
Forgetting to import HTTPException, which gives NameError: name 'HTTPException' is not defined.
Using `<=` instead of `<` in the bounds check, so the last+1 index still triggers an IndexError (500).
Writing the detail string without the f prefix, so it literally shows {item_id}.
Not restarting uvicorn (no --reload), so the old 500 behaviour persists.
Requesting an index that actually exists, so no 404 appears.

steps.title: List items with limit query parameter
steps.instructions: In main.py add `@app.get("/items")` with `list_items(limit: int = 10)` returning `items[0:limit]`. POST several items first, then run `curl -X GET 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?limit=3'` and check the JSON list it prints.

targets.caption: New list_items endpoint taking an integer limit query parameter
Request with limit=3 returns only the first 3 items

explanations.topic: Query parameters vs path parameters
FastAPI converts query strings to declared types (int)
Using limit to slice the list, default of 10
Same path, different HTTP method hits a different handler
Default value comes from the function signature

hints: Add a new function decorated with @app.get on the same "/items" path you used for POST.
Give the function a parameter `limit: int = 10`. FastAPI treats it as a query parameter automatically.
Return a slice of your list: `return items[0:limit]`.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to POST items after the server reloads, so the in-memory list is empty and returns []
Using @app.post instead of @app.get, so the request hits the create endpoint
Omitting the type hint, so limit stays a string and slicing raises a TypeError
Not quoting the URL in the shell, so the ? or & characters get interpreted by the shell
Giving the new function the same name as an existing handler

steps.title: Model items with Pydantic BaseModel
steps.instructions: In main.py import `BaseModel` from pydantic, define `class Item(BaseModel)` with `text: str` and `is_done: bool = False`, make create_item take `item: Item` and get_item return `-> Item`. POST JSON with `curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"text":"apple"}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/items`, then POST a body without `text` to see validation fail.

targets.caption: Pydantic model for a to-do item
Done flag defaults to False
Response is an object matching the model

explanations.topic: Why Pydantic models: structure, validation, docs, IDE completion
Modeled arguments are read from the JSON payload, not query params
Default values: is_done defaults to false
Removing a default makes a field required and validated

hints: Import BaseModel from pydantic and create a class that extends it with a text string and an is_done boolean.
Change create_item's parameter from a string to `item: Item`, and annotate get_item with `-> Item`.
The old query-parameter curl won't work now. Send JSON with -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"text":"apple"}' and drop ?item= from the URL.
To see validation, give `text` no default and send {"title":"apple"}. You should get a 422 with "missing".
common_mistakes: Still sending the item as a query parameter (?item=apple) instead of a JSON body, which gives a 422.
Forgetting the Content-Type: application/json header in curl.
Giving `text` a default value, so a body without text doesn't fail validation.
Writing `is_done: bool = false` (lowercase) instead of Python's `False`.
Using shell quoting that breaks the JSON on Windows cmd (single quotes don't work there).

steps.title: Declare response models on routes
steps.instructions: In main.py, add `response_model=Item` to the single-item GET decorator and `response_model=list[Item]` to the list GET decorator. Let uvicorn reload and confirm the endpoints still return Item-shaped JSON.

targets.caption: Single-item GET now declares its response shape
List GET declares a list of items

explanations.topic: Modeling the response, not just the request
response_model argument on the route decorator
Using list[Item] for endpoints returning many items
Response model as a contract for clients and interfaces

hints: The response shape is declared in the route decorator, not in the function body.
Add a keyword argument named response_model to @app.get(...), after the path string.
Use response_model=Item for /items/{item_id} and response_model=list[Item] for /items.
If list[Item] errors on an older Python version, import List from typing and use List[Item].
common_mistakes: Putting response_model on the function signature instead of inside the @app.get(...) decorator.
Writing response_model=Item on the list endpoint, so validation fails because a list is returned.
Spelling it responseModel or response_models.
Using list[Item] on a Python version older than 3.9 without importing List from typing.
Server not running with --reload, so the change isn't picked up.

steps.title: Test API in interactive docs
steps.instructions: With `uvicorn main:app --reload` running, open /docs, expand POST /items, click Try it out, edit the body and Execute. Also visit /redoc and /openapi.json to view the generated schema.

targets.caption: Add /docs to your server URL to open Swagger UI
Expand POST /items and click Try it out
Edit the request body, then Execute
The real response from your API
Link to the generated OpenAPI schema

explanations.topic: FastAPI generates interactive docs for free
Swagger UI shows endpoints, methods and parameters
Execute shows the curl command and sends the real request
ReDoc as an alternative documentation view
openapi.json describes all paths, schemas and responses

hints: Keep the uvicorn server running in your terminal, then go to your browser.
Click the POST /items row to expand it, press 'Try it out', edit the JSON body, then press 'Execute'.
Scroll down to 'Server response' to see the response body. Then try /redoc and /openapi.json.
common_mistakes: Stopping the uvicorn server before opening /docs, so the page doesn't load.
Forgetting to click 'Try it out', so the request body stays read-only.
Sending a request body whose fields don't match the Pydantic model, which returns 422 Unprocessable Entity.
Using a different port than the one uvicorn printed.
